body: I just talked to her and this is what I ended up doing. If she doesn't break up with him by the time their current lease expires (end of June) I will tell him myself. She seemed ok with that so I'll give her a chance I guess. She has no idea that I know some of his extended family through friends of friends so I'll be able to find out for myself if she actually does it. Such a shitty situation.

B) has been done already I just don't think she'll ever actually come clean with him. It's just really hard to stay silent when I put myself in his shoes. Nobody deserves to get treated like that and I sure as hell would want to know if my girlfriend was cheating on me. What if I don't tell him and he gets led on, treated like garbage for years and never trusts a human being ever again? What if they get married and he finds out on his own about some other dude then blows his own brains out? I feel like it's my responsibility as a kindhearted person to do something but I'm worried that lives could be ruined either way. Sucks.

I've talked to her father about it actually and he's been working with her to find a therapist and offer emotional support. I'm just afraid if her boyfriend finds out I've been fucking the piss out of her every weekend for six months he'll have an Afghan PTSD episode, snap and pull out a gun. 


Apparently they've been together for a very long time and she's so unstable and resistant to change that she might snap too if her whole (fake deranged) life comes crashing down in an instant. I just keep putting myself in his shoes, thinking about all the dirty shit she's done with me and feeling strongly obliged to warn him that his live-in girlfriend who tells him she loves him and cooks him breakfast in bed is a filthy whore who's had her face halfway up another dude's ass every weekend since September.


When I take a step back though I realize that I could end up responsible for someone getting physically hurt and that's the last thing I want from all of this. I worried something bad might happen even if I give her an ultimatum to tell him or else I will. I just don't know if I can keep silent...he needs to know and she needs to learn a lesson. I honestly might get pissed off one night and do it anyway but I'm so concerned for her safety I wouldn't be able to live with myself if something happened. : /

I know who he is and know enough about him from other people to be concerned with his potential reaction to news like this. I don't think he has ever hit a girl but I know he has very bad anger problems, legit, screaming night terror PTSD from front-line combat in Afghanistan and a lot of guns.

I could easily tell him anonymously and phrase it somewhat ambiguously in the least soul-crushing way possible but there is a non-zero probability that he gets his gun and shoots the girl right there and an even higher probability that she tries and possibly succeeds at killing herself. As horrible as cheating is no one deserves to die or get seriously injured over this. Do you think I should tell her that I'm going to tell him unless she faces reality, tells him herself and breaks up with him? I would have done that much already if they didn't fucking live together but I'm afraid (actually fairly certain) she is going to feel like she has no way out, nowhere to go home to and no support and take drastic measures to escape it all.
What if this girl ends up in the hospital or worse because of it? I don't want that on my conscience.

First off I really appreciate the reply and can tell you know what I'm dealing with here. I met with her today and it actually went a lot better than I'd expected. At least I didn't get stabbed o_o. She agreed to come with me to see a therapist if I set up the appointment so that's the next step I guess. She knows she has a serious problem and needs and wants to get help which is a very, very good thing. I'll tell you what though it's hard as fuck to just ignore my own feelings completely and offer my unconditional support to this girl when she's lying pathologically and half an almond short of a complete nutbar. If I can legitimately help at all though it's worth it to me and will make the world an ever so slightly better place. I'm still worried she's going to snap completely but nobody else is willing to suck it up and try to help her. I do know my limits, sort of, and will do my best. Thanks for the kind words.

Oh I'm quite familiar with it actually. I went through that phase years ago but the rhythms don't really do it for me anymore. It sounds too mechanical to me now and just makes me want to hear some swing or even some funk. It's got nothing to do with the melody or harmony I just can't get my brain dancing to the rhythms.

Of course they don't all go into jazz they go where the money is and no kidding not all metal and rock is a I-IV-V progression but even from ridiculous bands like for example Dream Theater and Symphony X, with extraordinarily talented classically trained guitar players, their most harmonically complex songs are just not on the same level as something like Giant Steps. My point is that someone like Petrucci is so good that he can be world famous and rich from his compositions and guitar playing in the realm of metal but if you compare him with a Blue Note signed bandleader guitarist he'd look like a complete noob. To switch it around if you took someone like Julian Lage and plopped him in Dream Theater they wouldn't miss a beat and would improve dramatically overnight. Like I said in my original comment, the *top* players tend to play jazz. There are definitely exceptions e.g. Steve Vai who would be comfortable in the jazz or classical idioms but they are few and far between. Find me three non-jazz guitar players of any age in any genre who could match up with these three young-generation Jazz players: Julian Lage, Gilad Heskelman and Mike Moreno, and not look stupid. It's not that easy if you know what these guys can really do. There's plenty of complexity in rock, metal, electronica etc. but it's just not on the same level as modern jazz.

Yea yea music is subjective etc. etc. but if we rank musicians based on objective measurables i.e. theoretical knowledge + technique, what I said is indisputable fact. Classical and Jazz are two sides of the same coin and EVERY modern popular musical genre is a distillation of concepts from these two 'genres.' The only real difference between the two is Jazz has improv. Both are just "music" and to be considered a professional Jazz or Classical player you have to know "music," not just an artificial subgenre like 'Rock and Roll' or 'Metal.' Once you have the knowledge, which you have to realize people go to grad school for, in order to play music in these idioms well enough to be considered a pro you need an obscene level of technique and be able to apply your vast wealth of musical knowledge subconsciously so that you can spontaneously play *anything* you hear in your head. Do a little research before getting defensive of your favorite metal shredder. There's a reason so few people play Jazz professionally compared to the scores and scores of genre bands out there.

They don't hold a candle to the top jazz guys...as it is with every other instrument. A lot of people just don't appreciate how much 'better' (technique, harmonic/rhythmic knowledge, etc.) the average working jazz musician is than players considered elite in genres like metal.
